digest.component_or_area: LLM gate telemetry and usage accounting
propositions: Gate run usage logs persist only token counts and request totals, omitting tool_calls, tool_calls_distinct, request_limit, tool_calls_limit, and finish_reason—data that is computed by failure_usage() but discarded at write time, making loop-vs-breadth distinguishability impossible from stored records

Local operator gate runs with no REBAR_USAGE_LOG env var set record nothing at all, despite being the primary use case where operators need tuning data, forcing re-instrumented runs to answer basic questions about budget consumption
The success path never computes tool-call shape via failure_usage(), leaving successful gate runs undebuggable for loop detection and preventing control-group comparisons against failed runs
Gate runs lack persisted wall-clock duration and ticket ID, preventing after-the-fact correlation between stored usage records and work context without re-running

Completion and plan-review gates are asymmetric in what they persist: completion verdict sidecar carries no counts/duration/limits while plan-review already carries per-call requests and metrics, leaving one gate blind

The fix wires the existing failure_usage() reducer into both success and failure paths, adds a default-on gate sink to .rebar/usage.jsonl, and augments summarize() rendering to make loop-vs-breadth ratios actionable without env-var setup
